correctness.rationale: With ||x||<1 put s=1-||x||² and R=I+xxᵀ/s. Direct expansion of R(D+Dᵀ)R reproduces exactly all three rank-one terms of Hall et al. Eq. (23), yielding 4J_B=R(D+Dᵀ)R. R is positive definite: vᵀRv=||v||²+(vᵀx)²/s and R⁻¹=I-xxᵀ. Sylvester congruence gives identical positive, zero and negative inertia for EVERY differentiable unital qubit Bloch generator, including nonsymmetric D. Thus any positive infinitesimal Bures/Fisher local direction exists iff λ_max(D+Dᵀ)>0, the source trace-distance criterion. For the diagonal illustrative D(t), tanh(t)<1 at every finite t, hence J_B<0 analytically at every interior state. Independently checked the full matrix identity and inverse by exact symbolic rationals for nonsymmetric-sign indefinite symmetric Q and rational x; this is corroboration of the all-parameter algebra, not the proof. Boundary ||x||=1, nonunital dynamics, integrated metric values and finite state-pair distances are not claimed.

originality.rationale: Hall et al. (2014) is the initiating primary source for both local witnesses; its Bures expression and trace-distance sign test are published and acknowledged, but the general invertible positive congruence, all-state inertia equivalence and the nonnumerical example conclusion are not stated in the inspected discussion. This does not assert that measuring integrated backflow yields identical values. Searches of published Resultary and Fisher-flow/non-unital Bures literature did not identify a dominating inertia theorem. Residual risk is a differently formulated metric-congruence observation; no failed search is treated as novelty proof.
residual_risks: A metric-tensor or contraction-rate identity equivalent to congruence could be published under terminology absent from searched results.
Only full-rank Bloch interior and differentiable unital dynamics; integrated/finitely separated and nonunital claims excluded.

value.rationale: This is more than a matrix-expansion exercise: it exactly answers whether two operationally distinct local information-backflow tests ever disagree on unital qubit dynamics, removes the need for a previously numerical negative-definiteness check, and cleanly delineates the nonunital and integrated-measure limitations. A future witness comparison needs precisely this all-state equivalence.
